title: Ashley Fehr
text:
I am a second year Complex Systems PhD student at the University of Vermont in Burlington, VT. I’m a member of the Computational Story Lab in the Vermont Complex Systems Institute where I work closely with Chris Danforth and Peter Dodds.
My main, broad interest is people in complex systems.
Graduation date ~ Spring 2028.

I am interested in measuring complex, interpersonal processes in digital mediums. People are motivated to socially connect and often rely on technology and text to do so—an often toneless medium. I wonder how well technology facilitates this goal and how can we best measure the constructs driving this process in individual and collective levels?
Enjoyable side quests include making accessible complexity research tools.







April: Presented a poster at the UVM Student Research Conference on statistical laws in conversation mediums.
March: Started POCS helpers, a draft of a package to provide principled, accessible complexity methods.
February: Passed a qualifying exam for the program (principles of complex systems).
January: Our team published the py-allotax tool to PyPi! We have a paper in progress describing our tool ecosystem for researching allometric systems.
January: Presented in Story Lab on spelunking among the natural and unnatural forms of conversation data and how these forms impact assumptions and limitations for working with corpora.





December: Presented in Student Complexity Research (and Pizza) Seminar on additional findings regarding Heap’s law in naturalistic conversation, individual movie conversations, and entire movie scripts.
November: Presented in Story Lab on measuring emergent statistical phenomena in conversations, using Heap’s law as an information theoretic starting point–focusing on CANDOR and the Movie-Dialogs corpus.
October: worked with a team to instantiate a python interface (py-allotax) to a Story Lab tool that performs complex analysis to plot rank divergences between 2 systems.
August: Passed a qualifying exam for the program (data science methods).
July: Attended IC2S2 at University of Pennsylvania.
May-June: Biked 560 miles (10k ft elevation) of the Empire State Trail over 9 days from Buffalo, NY to NYC.
May: Presented in Story Lab on linguistic coordination in the CANDOR conversation corpus.
April: Presented a poster at the UVM Student Research Conference on structuring discussion forum conversations as network data using a sample from Reddit.





August: Joined the Computational Story Lab and started in the PhD program in Complex Systems and Data Science.

title: Ashley Fehr
text:
Principles of complex systems helpers
This repository (in development) codes helpers for the purpose of making principled complexity methods quickly accessible. Examples include working with text, running a linear regression, or calculating and visualizing rank of types in a system.



Statistical laws in conversations
I am analyzing information scaling in conversations . The manuscript in progress demonstrates Zipf / Herdan-Heaps’ law in different kinds of conversations and goes beyond its general analysis to contribute new ways to statistically assess structures in conversations and contextualizing information scaling.


py-allotax
Working with the creators of the allotaxonometer, we implemented a python wrapper and interface around javascript implementation to compare 2 systems’ rankings of types. The Python py-allotax (published on PyPi) allows users to make allotaxonometric comparisons and plots programmatically. We have a paper in progress describing the allometric tool ecosystem.


Reddit as network data
I explored modeling Reddit posts as conversations and network data. Findings suggested that positive replies yields further discussion. Further, higher user activity can contribute to their rank rather than needing to be an influential user with high comment scores across Reddit.



Linguistic coordination
I assessed the representativeness of the CANDOR dataset to the U.S. population and analyzed the linguistic coordination of conversations  in CANDOR—how much speakers tailor their linguistic style in responses to the speaker, finding this effect also exists in stranger conversations.

title: Ashley Fehr
text: Before joining the Complex Systems PhD program, I worked in various roles as a research, applied, or data scientist. I applied my prior BA and MS education in psychology to behavioral science questions, conducting work ranging from survey data collection and analysis to representing people in simulations using agent based modeling. I became more interested in how to study and evaluate systems involving people, leading me to the area of complexity science!
